activities.caption: pair each term with what it does
activities.name: devBoundaryMatch

config.prompt: Pair each term with what it does:

pairs.right: violation of social norms — everywhere and constant
violation of codified law — a moving legal boundary
a folk devil, exaggerated media amplification, disproportionate response
mods and rockers, then muggers, then various drug users
public punishment, often designed for audiences rather than deterrence

config.why: Definitions track power and morality campaigns as much as harm — and the panic frequently manufactures the very deviance it fears.

activities.caption: place the peak of the curve on the age axis
activities.name: devAgePlace

config.prompt: Place the peak of the age-crime curve on the age axis:
config.why: Late teens, in every country and every decade measured — then a steep decline through the twenties; a small high-rate group accounts for a large share of offences.

config.text: Police-recorded numbers mix three things: actual offences, %%0%% willingness, and %%1%% practice. That is why criminologists anchor trend claims on %%2%% surveys — and why the dark figure of unreported and unrecorded crime is most of the %%3%%.
config.hint: Two verbs-turned-nouns, the survey type, and the metaphor.

activities.anchor: The first great spatial discovery came from mapping
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the Chicago finding
activities.name: devChicagoSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Shaw and McKay charted juvenile delinquency by Chicago neighbourhood.
Delinquency rates were stable by place, not by population.
Neighbourhoods kept high rates across decades of complete ethnic turnover.
That ruled out the neighbourhood itself and indicted the offenders' origins.
Social disorganisation: poverty, residential churn and mixed land use erode the networks that supervise teenagers.
config.correction: It ruled out the offenders' origins and indicted the neighbourhood itself — crime as a property of weak collective infrastructure.
config.why: The ecological demonstration — place effects separated from people effects — still organises the field.

activities.caption: pair each family with its mechanism
activities.name: devFamiliesMatch

config.prompt: Pair each family with its mechanism:

pairs.right: a single shared aim with rationed legitimate means; 'innovation' predicts precisely the recorded crime class
blocked youth form groups whose status systems invert the mainstream's
the puzzle is conformity: people refrain when bonds hold
attention shifts from the act to the reaction; closed doors push
marriage and steady work turn criminal careers off

config.why: Complementary in evidence: strain and subculture explain where offending starts, control what stops it, labelling what the system does afterwards.

activities.caption: true or false — the crime-drop decades
activities.name: devPerceptionJudge

statements.s: Measured crime fell steeply across the rich world from the early 1990s to the late 2010s.
statements.why: While disorder and anxiety were visible, the recorded trend ran the other way.

statements.s: US violent crime roughly halved over the same decades.
statements.why: And imprisonment rose through most of the prison surge.

statements.s: Imprisonment fell alongside offending during those decades.
statements.why: It rose — the two curves moved in opposite directions.

statements.s: Media amplification is a first-order variable, not background noise.
statements.why: Amplification is part of the mechanism, not decoration.

activities.caption: file each finding under its model
activities.name: devModelsSort

config.prompt: Three philosophies of responding to crime — file each finding:

items.label: emphasises incapacitation and desert — the US model
Norwegian prisons normalise life: keys, jobs, education
modest but consistent reoffending reductions, much higher victim satisfaction

config.why: Careful comparison forbids attributing the whole gap to prison style — but the pattern survives every adjustment so far.

activities.anchor: The evidence hierarchy for prevention, stated plainly
activities.caption: walk the trial results
activities.name: devPreventionBranch

config.root: A city has a violence problem and a budget line. Walk the trial results:

start.text: Option one: Scared Straight prison tours. What did the randomised trials find?

mis1.text: The Petrosino meta-analysis found the opposite: the programme increased offending.

ss.text: Option two: focused deterrence, Ceasefire-style — swift, certain, credible consequences plus real services for a small targeted group. Result?

choices.label: Youth homicides fell by roughly two-thirds

mis2.text: Certainty carries the effect — and the homicides fell by roughly two-thirds.

lead.text: And the surprise that teaches the most: lead abatement. Why does it count as crime policy?

choices.label: A toxin harming impulse control was, in effect, crime policy — phasing out leaded petrol preceded the crime declines
Lead causes crime directly in adults

mis3.text: The mechanism runs through childhood impulse control — the timing record and the econometrics back it.

end.text: Also on the works list: cognitive-behavioural programmes, hot-spots policing, therapeutic juvenile responses, summer jobs. Blanket severity and pure surveillance without legitimacy do not make it.

config.why: Certainty beats severity; legitimacy does work fear cannot — and responses are causes, audited like anything else.
